clue.text: Prelate has place on board next to royalty

definitions.meaning: a senior churchman such as one in charge of a diocese

definitions.text: place on board next to royalty
definitions.meaning: on a chessboard this piece starts beside the king and queen

explanation.surface: A senior cleric sits on a company board alongside members of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a company board; it is the chessboard, where the piece begins next to the king and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a senior clergyman and the diagonal-moving chess piece that stands beside the royal pieces.

clue.text: Odds on girl's beginning to enjoy ball?

parts.note: SP, the starting price, gives the betting odds in racing
the possessive of a girl is her

indicators.note: the first letter of the word enjoy is its beginning

explanation.surface: A bettor asks about the odds on a young woman starting to have fun at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue means stacked above. 'ball' looks like a dance but is a round object.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a round solid, the everyday example of a globe-shaped form.

clue.text: Weirdly eccentric kind of swindle

indicators.note: done weirdly means the letters of the following words are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: An oddball sort of fraud is described as strangely unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weirdly' rearranges all fifteen letters of ECCENTRIC KIND OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A con in which the victim's trust is won and then exploited is a classic fraud.

clue.text: Straight path to buzz along?

parts.note: the direct route an insect that buzzes would fly

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a direct route for zipping along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzz' points to the insect said to fly straight back to its hive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the most direct route, named after the insect's supposed straight flight home.

clue.text: Showing bad posture, delivery route burden being taken on?

parts.note: a milkman's or paperboy's round is the route of deliveries
a burden shouldered is one taken on

explanation.surface: A delivery worker slumps from the weight of carrying heavy loads on the route.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooping with the upper back curved forward is a common sign of poor posture.

clue.text: Are going to recreate period style

indicators.note: to recreate means the letters of the preceding words are built anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Designers plan to revive a historic look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recreate' shuffles the letters of ARE GOING.
explanation.definitionFit: The architecture and furniture of 1714 to 1830, the reigns of four Kings George, form a recognised period style.

clue.text: That short? Not any more

definitions.meaning: read literally, not greater in length, so of exactly that brevity
having ceased, no more at present

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the phrase literally as 'not of greater length'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly but not now, and literally says something is not lengthier, hence that short.

clue.text: One's parking-took car round to show invalid

indicators.note: round means the past-tense driving word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to take the car is to drive, past tense drove
one is I, so one's becomes I'S, read as is
P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone's parking spot ended when they drove around to show something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as I'S, a crossword trick; 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute an argument is to prove it false or invalid.

clue.text: Fairy king gives medal to chap

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour awarded with a medal
Ron is a typical man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A fairy monarch awards a decoration to a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream the ruler of the fairies is married to Titania.

clue.text: Native of Australia millions in Europe

indicators.note: in means the millions letter sits within the Europe letters

parts.note: EU, the European Union, stands for Europe

explanation.surface: An Australian national's millions are banked in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless bird is found only in Australia, so it is a native there.

clue.text: Happy church always nearly packed out

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

indicators.note: nearly means the word for packed out loses its last letter

parts.note: packed out means full

explanation.surface: A church that is always almost full makes everyone happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the final L of FULL, leaving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good spirits and upbeat is what being glad or happy means.

clue.text: New missile is limited

parts.note: an arrow is a missile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A newly developed missile has a restricted range.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restricted in scope or breadth is called slim or confined.

clue.text: Excited passenger is down to take new flights

indicators.note: excited means the letters of the following words are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: An agitated airline traveller is feeling low about catching new flights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' rearranges the fifteen letters of PASSENGER IS DOWN. 'flights' suggests air travel but means new ventures.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to try something new and independent, as a young bird first tries flying.

clue.text: Line, say, of deer

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and gives a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A line of deer is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives the sound of ROW (a line), which is ROE.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe is a small species of European and Asian deer.

clue.text: Porthole in launch?

definitions.meaning: a gap in a ship's side to let in light and air
the start or debut of something

explanation.surface: A ship's window is fitted during its launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' suggests ship launching, matching the porthole, but here it means a debut.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an aperture or gap and the first night or start of something.

clue.text: In pure chaos, no record of introduction

indicators.note: In means the record pieces are placed within the jumbled letters
chaos means the letters of the word pure are thrown into disorder

parts.note: no can be nil, shown by the letter O
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: In utter confusion, there is no account of how things began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' makes PRUE; 'In' is the container signal; 'no' as nil gives the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening section of a play or book is its preface or introduction.

clue.text: Name of little streams is straightforward

parts.note: rills are small brooks

explanation.surface: Naming small brooks is a simple matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and basic, without extras or ornament, is what simple and unfussy means.

clue.text: Reckoning to take railway in rural area

indicators.note: to take means the reckoning word collects the railway letters after it

parts.note: a count is a reckoning or tally

explanation.surface: Someone calculates whether to take the train out to the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Land away from towns, farmland and villages, is the rural landscape.

clue.text: Time to take little house, even if small

indicators.note: to take means the time letter collects the house letters after it

parts.note: HO is the short form of house

explanation.surface: Someone needs time to buy a cottage, even if it is tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' signals the shortened informal spelling of the conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the abbreviated spelling of although, meaning even if.

clue.text: Tragic hero gives protective garment to girl

parts.note: a mac is a mackintosh, a raincoat
Beth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tragic figure presents a raincoat to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: MAC is British slang for a raincoat (a mackintosh).
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Scottish king is the doomed protagonist of his tragedy.

clue.text: Volume available at drinks time?

parts.note: a large illustrated book left on the low table where hot drinks are served

explanation.surface: A book is on hand when refreshments are served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks time' points to the hot drink and the low table it is set on, where such books lie for browsing.
explanation.definitionFit: A big glossy picture book displayed for guests to browse in a living room.

clue.text: Rolls out of this shop

parts.note: bread rolls come out of the shop that bakes them

explanation.surface: Something rolls out of a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like a verb but is the noun, bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop where bread and buns are baked and sold.

clue.text: Pearl set in fixed relationship?

definitions.meaning: a pearl of fine lustre, or that lustre itself
to position something relative to compass points or surroundings

explanation.walkthrough: The jeweller's sense, a lustrous pearl, is uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a pearl of great lustre; as a verb, to align or position relative to something.

clue.text: Firm support for office equipment

parts.note: CO, company, is a firm
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge

explanation.surface: A company provides support for office machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopying machine is standard office equipment.

clue.text: Give up wickedness, as burglar does?

parts.note: to break a habit is to give it up
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: A criminal is urged to give up his wicked ways, yet burgles.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BREAK SIN the letters mean give up wickedness; the burglar enters by force.
explanation.definitionFit: A housebreaker forces entry into a building illegally.

clue.text: Sweet nicely presented

indicators.note: presented means the letters are displayed within the word nicely

explanation.surface: A dessert is attractively plated.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'nICEly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert such as a water ice or ice cream counts as a sweet, the British word for pudding.

clue.text: But such a school is private

definitions.text: But such a school is private

parts.words: But such a school is private
parts.note: in Britain, the fee-paying elite schools such as Eton are called by the opposite of private

explanation.surface: A paradox about a type of school that is not open to all.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is an old independent, fee-paying school such as Eton, so it is in fact private.
explanation.definitionFit: The British term for an elite fee-charging independent school uses the word that normally means open to all.

clue.text: Elder's age known in this circle

definitions.text: Elder's age known in this circle

parts.words: Elder's age known in this circle
parts.note: the elder is a shrub whose years can be counted from annual growth bands in its trunk

explanation.surface: An older person's age is common knowledge among their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' suggests an older person; it is the elder tree, and 'circle' is a growth band, not a social group.
explanation.definitionFit: Each annual band of growth in a trunk's cross-section marks one year, so counting them gives its age.
